outline.text:
You have now reached the end of this school physics course.
You have studied different kinds of motion, as well as the structure and properties of bodies.
Scientists around the world have explored these questions for centuries, and your own studies have brought you into that exploration.

Physics helps us understand laws that apply across a wide range of natural phenomena.
These laws let us explain events around us and investigate processes throughout the universe.

Physics seeks shared laws of nature and uses them to explain particular processes.
As research advances, scientists connect many phenomena into an overall picture.
Events in the world are not isolated from one another: its rich variety of phenomena is connected.

**The mechanical picture of the world** Newtonian mechanics gave scientists an impressive, orderly picture of the world.
In its account of Newton's ideas, the textbook says that the world consists of "solid, weighty, impenetrable, moving particles."
It also describes these particles as "absolutely solid. They are incomparably harder than the bodies made from them, so hard that they never wear out or break into smaller pieces."

In this historical picture, particles differ mainly in mass, and different particle motions explain the variety of bodies.
Their internal properties take a secondary place.
These statements describe a model of the time, not modern conclusions about the structure of microscopic particles.

Newton's laws of motion formed the basis of this mechanical picture.
They accurately describe many motions, from those of celestial bodies to grains of sand carried by the wind.

Mechanics also helps us study wind, since air consists of particles.
This accuracy has limits: Newtonian mechanics works well for many macroscopic processes at speeds far below the speed of light, but it is not a universally exact account of microscopic or high-speed motion.

For a long time, scientists believed that Newtonian mechanics supplied nature's unified basic laws.
The textbook attributes this remark to Lagrange, a scientist in France: "There is no one happier than Newton, because he alone, on one occasion, had the good fortune to draw a picture of the world."

Research into electromagnetic phenomena showed that Newtonian mechanics alone could not provide a complete explanation.
The simple mechanical picture had limits.
This did not mean that mechanics could never describe the motion of bodies subject to electromagnetic forces.

Maxwell established fundamental laws describing electromagnetic fields.
These laws could not be derived from Newtonian mechanics alone, so fields had to become part of the physical picture.

**The electromagnetic picture of the world** In the Newtonian model of gravity, bodies exert gravitational effects across empty space instantaneously, an example of action at a distance.
Electrodynamics changed how scientists understood electromagnetic interactions.

Charged bodies produce electromagnetic fields, and electromagnetic effects are transmitted through those fields.
Changes in the field propagate at a finite speed instead of reaching distant places instantly.
The textbook calls this field-mediated picture local action.

Electromagnetic interactions occur throughout nature because atoms contain charged particles.
They contribute to interactions within atoms and molecules and between molecules in macroscopic bodies.

Electromagnetic effects also occur inside nuclei, but the main interaction binding a nucleus is the strong interaction, not electromagnetism.
We encounter electromagnetic effects both over very small distances and in the radiation emitted by celestial bodies.

The success of electrodynamics encouraged attempts to build **a unified electromagnetic picture of the world**.
Scientists hoped to explain all bodies through the laws of electromagnetic interaction.
This was a historical attempt at unification, not a complete explanation established by modern physics.

The textbook presents special relativity as a high point in the development of the electromagnetic picture.
It clarified the importance of finite propagation speeds and changed our understanding of space and time.

When motion can no longer be treated as slow compared with light, relativistic laws are needed.
Under suitable low-speed conditions, Newtonian mechanics remains a good approximation.
The success of relativity does not mean that every interaction is electromagnetic.

When the mechanical picture was dominant, scientists tried to explain electromagnetic phenomena as mechanical processes in a special medium called the world ether.
Later, they tried the reverse approach: deriving the motion of material particles from electromagnetic theory and even imagining particles as "condensations" of the electromagnetic field.
Both ideas belong to the historical search for a unified explanation.

These efforts did not reduce every natural process to electromagnetism.
Electromagnetic field theory alone does not provide all laws of particle motion or a theory of gravity.
The discovery of electrically neutral particles and other interactions also showed that nature was more complex than the simple electromagnetic picture.

A single electromagnetic force cannot explain every process.
This is not a proof that a more unified theory is impossible.
It shows that the existing picture is incomplete.

**The common structure of matter** Bodies in the world are diverse, yet ordinary matter shares basic constituents.
Ordinary matter in celestial bodies and on Earth contains the same kinds of atoms.

An atom does not become a different kind simply because it is in a different place.
This does not mean that all atoms are identical or that every celestial body has the same composition.
Atoms in living organisms obey the same physical laws as atoms in nonliving matter.

Atoms share a basic structure: electrons surround a nucleus made of protons and, usually, neutrons.
The most common kind of hydrogen atom has no neutron in its nucleus.

The textbook's three basic particles are the three familiar atomic constituents: protons, neutrons and electrons.
In modern terminology, protons and neutrons are made of quarks and are not elementary particles.

The electromagnetic field describes the electromagnetic interaction between a nucleus and its electrons.
Its quantum is the photon.
Quantum theory is needed to describe electrons in atoms, rather than treating them as little planets following fixed paths around a nucleus.

The textbook uses the exchange of $\pi$ mesons to explain interactions between protons and neutrons in a nucleus.
In modern physics, this is a nuclear-force model valid within a particular low-energy range, not a description of a single elementary quantum of a universal nuclear field.
A deeper account of the strong interaction involves quarks and gluons, and mesons are themselves composite particles.

In this decay, a free neutron becomes a proton and emits an electron and an electron antineutrino.
The textbook says neutrino here, but this particular process requires an electron antineutrino.

Many other particles have been discovered, some requiring high-energy collisions for their production.
Their importance depends on the process being studied, not solely on extremely high energies.

During the first half of the twentieth century, scientists increasingly discovered that particles could be created, disappear or undergo transformations in interactions.
The textbook summarizes this by saying that "all elementary particles can transform into one another."

More precisely, allowed transformations must satisfy conservation requirements, including those for energy and electric charge.
This does not allow an arbitrary particle to turn into any other particle on its own.

Discoveries of particles and their transformations gave the common structure of matter a more prominent place in the unified picture.
The textbook interprets different elementary particles as different concrete forms in which matter exists.

This is its statement about the unity of matter.
The specific properties and transformations of particles still require theoretical and experimental study.

**The modern physical picture of the world** Nature's shared features are not limited to the constituents of matter.
They also appear in the common laws describing particle motion and interactions.

Modern physics distinguishes four known fundamental interactions: **gravity, electromagnetism, the strong interaction and the weak interaction**.
The textbook's nuclear force is a manifestation of the strong interaction between nucleons, not an additional fundamental force.
The weak interaction contributes to certain particle decays and transformations, but its effects are not limited to those processes.

From the universe and Earth to living organisms, atoms and nuclei, studying a system requires considering its relevant interactions.
The four interactions do not all dominate every process together.
Their importance depends on the system and its conditions.

The discovery of quantum properties profoundly changed the classical physical picture.
Quantum physics, which describes microscopic particles, added new elements to our understanding of nature's shared laws.

Quantum physics makes an absolute division between discontinuous material particles and continuous fields inadequate.
The quantum of the electromagnetic field is the photon.
The textbook's $\pi$ mesons can describe nucleon interactions within a limited range, but they are not elementary quanta of a fundamental nuclear field in the modern sense.

Light and material particles can show wave-like effects such as interference and particle-like behaviour in detection, commonly called **wave-particle duality**.
This does not mean that a microscopic object switches between being a classical little ball and a classical wave.
Neither single classical picture fully describes quantum phenomena.

Quantum theory gives probabilities for possible measurement outcomes and explains wave-like and particle-like behaviour within one framework.
In the usual quantum theory, an isolated system's state evolves according to a deterministic equation.

Probabilities do not mean that everything is lawless.
Some measurements have a definite result for a particular state, but in general we cannot predict with certainty which result a single measurement will give.

Quantum theory provides a common framework for describing microscopic particle motion, interactions and transformations.
This does not mean that it already explains every natural phenomenon.
Fully combining gravity with quantum theory remains an unsolved problem.

Physics has found shared laws behind many natural phenomena, but the unified picture remains incomplete.
Why these different particles exist, and why they have particular masses, charges and other properties, still raises questions for research.

Many particle properties must be determined experimentally.
The modern Standard Model connects some particles and interactions, but does not provide a complete unified explanation including gravity.

When the textbook was written, scientists anticipated major discoveries and considered whether a deeper theory might explain particle properties.
That expectation is not evidence that a discovery is imminent.
We cannot predict here whether a more complete theory will take years or decades to develop.

The textbook closes with words it attributes to Galileo: "Such deep mysteries and such profound meanings lie hidden here that even a few hundred of the keenest thinkers, working one after another for several thousand years, have not penetrated them. The joy of creative exploration and discovery still remains."
It places these words three hundred and fifty years before its own time and says that their spirit of inquiry has not become outdated.

flow.source_text: 核中质子和中子之间的相互作用基本上是由 $\pi$ 介子实现的，它是核场的量子. 当中子衰变时，产生中微子. 此外，还发现了许多其他基本粒子. 但仅仅在能量极大的粒子相互作用时，它们才开始起显著的作用.

flow.text:
In this decay, a free neutron becomes a proton and emits an electron and an electron antineutrino.
The textbook says neutrino here, but this particular process requires an electron antineutrino.
flow.source_text: 核中质子和中子之间的相互作用基本上是由 $\pi$ 介子实现的，它是核场的量子. 当中子衰变时，产生中微子. 此外，还发现了许多其他基本粒子. 但仅仅在能量极大的粒子相互作用时，它们才开始起显著的作用.

flow.text:
Many other particles have been discovered, some requiring high-energy collisions for their production.
Their importance depends on the process being studied, not solely on extremely high energies.
flow.source_text: 核中质子和中子之间的相互作用基本上是由 $\pi$ 介子实现的，它是核场的量子. 当中子衰变时，产生中微子. 此外，还发现了许多其他基本粒子. 但仅仅在能量极大的粒子相互作用时，它们才开始起显著的作用.

flow.text:
During the first half of the twentieth century, scientists increasingly discovered that particles could be created, disappear or undergo transformations in interactions.
The textbook summarizes this by saying that "all elementary particles can transform into one another."
flow.source_text: 在二十世纪上半叶发现了一个有重大意义的事实：**所有的基本粒子都能够互相转化**.

flow.text:
More precisely, allowed transformations must satisfy conservation requirements, including those for energy and electric charge.
This does not allow an arbitrary particle to turn into any other particle on its own.
flow.source_text: 在二十世纪上半叶发现了一个有重大意义的事实：**所有的基本粒子都能够互相转化**.

flow.text:
Discoveries of particles and their transformations gave the common structure of matter a more prominent place in the unified picture.
The textbook interprets different elementary particles as different concrete forms in which matter exists.
flow.source_text: 在基本粒子和它们的转化被发现后，物质结构的统一性被提到世界统一图景的首要地位. 所有基本粒子的物质性是这个统一性的基础. **各种不同的基本粒子是物质存在的各种不同的具体形式**.

flow.text:
This is its statement about the unity of matter.
The specific properties and transformations of particles still require theoretical and experimental study.
flow.source_text: 在基本粒子和它们的转化被发现后，物质结构的统一性被提到世界统一图景的首要地位. 所有基本粒子的物质性是这个统一性的基础. **各种不同的基本粒子是物质存在的各种不同的具体形式**.

flow.text:
**The modern physical picture of the world** Nature's shared features are not limited to the constituents of matter.
They also appear in the common laws describing particle motion and interactions.
flow.source_text: **世界现代物理图景** 世界的统一不仅仅是物质结构的统一. 这个统一也表现在粒子运动定律和它们的相互作用定律中.

flow.text:
Modern physics distinguishes four known fundamental interactions: **gravity, electromagnetism, the strong interaction and the weak interaction**.
The textbook's nuclear force is a manifestation of the strong interaction between nucleons, not an additional fundamental force.
The weak interaction contributes to certain particle decays and transformations, but its effects are not limited to those processes.
flow.source_text: 尽管物体间相互作用的多样化是惊人的，但根据现代的资料在自然界中只有四种力，这就是**引力、电磁力、核力**及**弱相互作用**. 最后一种力只在基本粒子彼此转化时才表现为主要的. 我们在广阔无限的宇宙中，在地球上，在任何物体中(包括活的机体)，在原子和原子核中，在基本粒子的所有转化中都会遇到以上四种力.

flow.text:
From the universe and Earth to living organisms, atoms and nuclei, studying a system requires considering its relevant interactions.
The four interactions do not all dominate every process together.
Their importance depends on the system and its conditions.
flow.source_text: 尽管物体间相互作用的多样化是惊人的，但根据现代的资料在自然界中只有四种力，这就是**引力、电磁力、核力**及**弱相互作用**. 最后一种力只在基本粒子彼此转化时才表现为主要的. 我们在广阔无限的宇宙中，在地球上，在任何物体中(包括活的机体)，在原子和原子核中，在基本粒子的所有转化中都会遇到以上四种力.

flow.text:
The discovery of quantum properties profoundly changed the classical physical picture.
Quantum physics, which describes microscopic particles, added new elements to our understanding of nature's shared laws.
flow.source_text: 对世界物理图景的经典概念的革命性变革是在发现了物质的量子特性以后发生的. 描写微观粒子运动的量子物理出现以后，世界统一物理图景的新因素就开始出现了.

flow.text:
Quantum physics makes an absolute division between discontinuous material particles and continuous fields inadequate.
The quantum of the electromagnetic field is the photon.
The textbook's $\pi$ mesons can describe nucleon interactions within a limited range, but they are not elementary quanta of a fundamental nuclear field in the modern sense.
flow.source_text: 把物质分成具有不连续结构的实体和连续的场就失去了绝对的意义. 每一个场都有相应于该场的量子，电磁场有光子，核场有 $\pi$ 介子等等. 并且所有的粒子都具有波动性. **所有形式的物质都具有波粒二象性**.

flow.text:
Light and material particles can show wave-like effects such as interference and particle-like behaviour in detection, commonly called **wave-particle duality**.
This does not mean that a microscopic object switches between being a classical little ball and a classical wave.
Neither single classical picture fully describes quantum phenomena.
flow.source_text: 把物质分成具有不连续结构的实体和连续的场就失去了绝对的意义. 每一个场都有相应于该场的量子，电磁场有光子，核场有 $\pi$ 介子等等. 并且所有的粒子都具有波动性. **所有形式的物质都具有波粒二象性**.

flow.text:
Quantum theory gives probabilities for possible measurement outcomes and explains wave-like and particle-like behaviour within one framework.
In the usual quantum theory, an isolated system's state evolves according to a deterministic equation.
flow.source_text: 由于所有的微观粒子的运动规律都具有统计(几率)性，因而可以在某个理论的范围内用似乎互相对立的微粒性与波动性来描述. 这个事实使得对于微观物体不可能做出这种或那种单值状态的预言.

flow.text:
Probabilities do not mean that everything is lawless.
Some measurements have a definite result for a particular state, but in general we cannot predict with certainty which result a single measurement will give.
flow.source_text: 由于所有的微观粒子的运动规律都具有统计(几率)性，因而可以在某个理论的范围内用似乎互相对立的微粒性与波动性来描述. 这个事实使得对于微观物体不可能做出这种或那种单值状态的预言.

flow.text:
Quantum theory provides a common framework for describing microscopic particle motion, interactions and transformations.
This does not mean that it already explains every natural phenomenon.
Fully combining gravity with quantum theory remains an unsolved problem.
flow.source_text: 量子理论的原则是描写所有粒子的运动和粒子之间的相互作用及相互转变的普遍的原则.

flow.text:
Physics has found shared laws behind many natural phenomena, but the unified picture remains incomplete.
Why these different particles exist, and why they have particular masses, charges and other properties, still raises questions for research.
flow.source_text: 因而，现代物理以确凿的证据向我们显示了自然界的统一性. 但终究目前还是有很多东西，甚至就是世界统一的物理实质本身也还没有发现. 现在还不知道，为什么各种不同的基本微粒是如此之多，为什么它们具有一定的质量、电量及其它特性？ 至今所有这些数值都是用实验测出的. 不同类型的相互作用间的联系现在才开始描绘. 我们现在大概是处在新的伟大发明的前夜. 如果为了描述原子中粒子的运动需要建立具有特殊规律的量子力学，则为了建立解释粒子所有特性的基本粒子统一理论，就可能需要更加根本的理论. 现在无法肯定这一点要过几年还是几十年才能实现.

flow.text:
Many particle properties must be determined experimentally.
The modern Standard Model connects some particles and interactions, but does not provide a complete unified explanation including gravity.
flow.source_text: 因而，现代物理以确凿的证据向我们显示了自然界的统一性. 但终究目前还是有很多东西，甚至就是世界统一的物理实质本身也还没有发现. 现在还不知道，为什么各种不同的基本微粒是如此之多，为什么它们具有一定的质量、电量及其它特性？ 至今所有这些数值都是用实验测出的. 不同类型的相互作用间的联系现在才开始描绘. 我们现在大概是处在新的伟大发明的前夜. 如果为了描述原子中粒子的运动需要建立具有特殊规律的量子力学，则为了建立解释粒子所有特性的基本粒子统一理论，就可能需要更加根本的理论. 现在无法肯定这一点要过几年还是几十年才能实现.

flow.text:
When the textbook was written, scientists anticipated major discoveries and considered whether a deeper theory might explain particle properties.
That expectation is not evidence that a discovery is imminent.
We cannot predict here whether a more complete theory will take years or decades to develop.
flow.source_text: 因而，现代物理以确凿的证据向我们显示了自然界的统一性. 但终究目前还是有很多东西，甚至就是世界统一的物理实质本身也还没有发现. 现在还不知道，为什么各种不同的基本微粒是如此之多，为什么它们具有一定的质量、电量及其它特性？ 至今所有这些数值都是用实验测出的. 不同类型的相互作用间的联系现在才开始描绘. 我们现在大概是处在新的伟大发明的前夜. 如果为了描述原子中粒子的运动需要建立具有特殊规律的量子力学，则为了建立解释粒子所有特性的基本粒子统一理论，就可能需要更加根本的理论. 现在无法肯定这一点要过几年还是几十年才能实现.

flow.text:
The textbook closes with words it attributes to Galileo: "Such deep mysteries and such profound meanings lie hidden here that even a few hundred of the keenest thinkers, working one after another for several thousand years, have not penetrated them. The joy of creative exploration and discovery still remains."
It places these words three hundred and fifty years before its own time and says that their spirit of inquiry has not become outdated.
flow.source_text: “这里面隐藏着这样深的秘密和这样高的涵义，以至于虽然有几百位最机敏的思想家相继工作了数千年之久，也没有洞察这些秘密和涵义. 创造性地探索和发现的愉快仍然存在着”. 伽里略三百五十年前说的这些话，至今一点也没有过时.
